passages.provision_quote: A person who is prohibited from possessing a firearm under the laws of this state, except under Section 29610, who purchases, owns, or possesses body armor, as defined in Section 16288, except as authorized under subdivision (c), is guilty of a misdemeanor.
passages.note: Authored bill regulates body armor possession by persons already barred from firearms; it sets no rule on who may own, buy or carry a firearm, which is the dimension the rungs separate.

rows.reasoning: The only source is Connolly's authored AB 92 (2023-2024), which makes it "a misdemeanor for a person who is prohibited from possessing a firearm under the laws of this state to purchase, own, or possess body armor" — a collateral rule about body armor for people already barred from guns. It speaks to none of the clauses the rungs turn on (banning civilian ownership, banning semi-automatic assault-style weapons, universal background checks on every sale, loosening carry rules, or permitless carry), so no passage survives V2.
